root_cause: The #3843 snapshot recovery correctly identified 15 production-applied identities beyond the prior 568-entry lock, but production then advanced by eight LinkedIn organization-OAuth migrations through 20261006103856 outside canonical Git lineage. Leaving the recovery target frozen at 583 would therefore preserve current repository-to-production drift even though the original snapshot was repaired.
prevention: Keep the canonical repository migration lock equal to the current observed production migration ledger, not only an historical merge snapshot; current target is 591 identities through 20261006103856.

Restore every already-applied production statement as an immutable repository mirror and allow historical security exemption only at its exact reviewed Git blob SHA; any byte edit restores fail-closed security checking.
Classify Supabase Preview as not applicable only when every database-relevant changed source is an exact registered historical production mirror; ordinary migrations still require provider preview.
Treat supabase/migration-history.lock.json as non-executable metadata while requiring applied.length = production_ledger_count = current production ledger count.
Prevent recurrence by making protected main the only authority for future Supabase production promotion; direct chat, agent or provider deployment must not create new production-only lineage.

evaluation.expected: Repository history and migration-history.lock.json represent all 591 currently applied production migrations; historical mirrors are exact-blob bound and preview/security stay fail-closed for any non-mirror database change.
